This option may only be set when rendering GIFs. It determines how many frames are rendered, while the other ones get skipped in order to lower the FPS of the GIF. For example, if the `fps` is 30, and `everyNthFrame` is 2, the FPS of the GIF is `15`.

## CLI flag

```text
--every-nth-frame <value>
```

The following CLI commands accept this option:

- [`remotion studio`](/docs/cli/studio)
- [`remotion render`](/docs/cli/render)
- [`remotion benchmark`](/docs/cli/benchmark)
- [`remotion lambda render`](/docs/lambda/cli/render)
- [`remotion cloudrun render`](/docs/cloudrun/cli/render)

## APIs that have this option

The following APIs accept this option:

- [`renderMediaOnCloudrun()`](/docs/cloudrun/rendermediaoncloudrun#everynthframe)
- [`renderMediaOnLambda()`](/docs/lambda/rendermediaonlambda#everynthframe)
- [`combineChunks()`](/docs/renderer/combine-chunks#everynthframe)
- [`renderFrames()`](/docs/renderer/render-frames#everynthframe)
- [`renderMedia()`](/docs/renderer/render-media#everynthframe)

## Config file

```ts twoslash title="remotion.config.ts"
import {Config} from '@remotion/cli/config';
// ---cut---
Config.setEveryNthFrame(2);
```
